clinical_effect: Low-dose naproxen was observed to interfere with the antiplatelet effect of low-dose immediate-release aspirin.
evidence_quote: lower dose naproxen (220mg/day or 220mg twice daily) interfered with the antiplatelet effect of low-dose immediate-release aspirin

clinical_effect: Co-use of an NSAID with serotonin-reuptake-interfering agents may increase bleeding risk.
evidence_quote: concomitant use of drugs that interfere with serotonin reuptake and an NSAID may potentiate the risk of bleeding more than an NSAID alone.

clinical_effect: Naproxen and anticoagulants such as warfarin have a synergistic bleeding effect.
evidence_quote: Naproxen and anticoagulants such as warfarin have a synergistic effect on bleeding.

clinical_effect: Sertraline plus antiplatelet agents or anticoagulants may increase bleeding risk.
evidence_quote: The concurrent use of an antiplatelet agent or anticoagulant with sertraline hydrochloride may potentiate the risk of bleeding.

clinical_effect: Sertraline with MAOIs increases serotonin syndrome risk; coadministration is contraindicated.
evidence_quote: Sertraline hydrochloride is contraindicated in patients taking MAOIs

clinical_effect: Sertraline with pimozide is contraindicated; the cited passage discusses increased pimozide exposure and QTc risk.
evidence_quote: Concomitant use of pimozide and sertraline hydrochloride is contraindicated

clinical_effect: Sertraline with warfarin is associated with bleeding concerns; carefully monitor INR.
evidence_quote: For patients taking warfarin, carefully monitor the international normalized ratio

clinical_effect: CYP2C9/CYP1A2/CYP3A4 inducers may decrease warfarin exposure and INR.
evidence_quote: Inducers of CYP2C9, 1A2, and/or 3A4 have the potential to decrease the effect (decrease INR) of warfarin by decreasing the exposure of warfarin.

clinical_effect: CYP2C9/CYP1A2/CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase warfarin exposure and INR.
evidence_quote: Inhibitors of CYP2C9, 1A2, and/or 3A4 have the potential to increase the effect (increase INR) of warfarin by increasing the exposure of warfarin.
